If a continuous family of parameter values gives the same prediction for every observable, no
data of these observables can tell the members apart. `symmetryDetection()`, through the Python
package [symident](https://dmodverse.github.io/symident/), finds such families in the model of
[Setting up models](guide-model.html); they are removed before the fit. Code: `symmetries.R` and
the end of `model.R`.

## Lie symmetries and detection

Such a family is the orbit of a Lie symmetry with a generator, a vector field on the parameters.
Most symmetries of reaction networks are scalings: the moved parameters are multiplied by powers
of one factor, and on log scale an orbit is a straight line. symident obtains the generators as
the kernel of the observability-identifiability matrix, built from the Lie derivatives of the
observables, and proves scalings exactly; see
[Methods > Structural identifiability and Lie symmetries](methods-symmetries.html).

## Detection settings

- `equilibrate = TRUE`: the cells start at the steady state without TNFα, so initial values are
  functions of the parameters.
- `reduceCQ = TRUE`: one species per conserved moiety is eliminated, symmetries act on the totals,
  the parameters of `Pimpl()`.
- `forcings = "TNF"`: TNFα is an input state, 0 at rest and set by the event at time 0.
- `conditions`: the two doses; a direction is non-identifiable only if it is so in both.

The imaging readouts bleach, $y = \log(s x + o) - \tau t$; $e^{-\tau t}$ is no function of the
states of a model at rest. In the control the states are constant and the slope of an imaging
readout is $-\tau$ alone, so the bleaching rates are in no symmetry, and `symmetries.R` drops the
bleaching terms.

## Symmetries of the full model

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/symmetries.rds", "symmetries.R"))
invisible(stored("results/reduction.rds", "symmetries.R"))
```

```{r symmetries, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
symmetries <- readRDS("results/symmetries.rds")
symmetries
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
types <- vapply(symmetries$symmetries, `[[`, "", "type")
```

The rank of the observability-identifiability matrix is `r symmetries$rank` of
`r symmetries$dim` coordinates, proven; the kernel is spanned by
`r inWords(length(types))` scalings, each proven over the rationals. The `r inWords(length(types))` printed generators
are one basis, sums of them are symmetries too. Up to such sums there are four kinds.

- **Unobserved intermediates.** Active receptor `TNFR`, IκBα transcript `mIkb`, A20 transcript and
  A20 protein are unmeasured, A20 only up to a scale. Each acts through the product of level and
  driven rate constant: level and production rate times $\lambda$, driven rate divided by
  $\lambda$. $X_1$: receptor (`uptake`, `act_Ikk_by_TNF`); $X_4$: IκBα transcript
  (`prod_mIkb_by_nNfk`, `prod_Ikb`); $X_6$: A20 transcript (`build_RnaA20`, `build_A20`). $X_7$
  moves A20 with the A20 production, the IKK inhibition constant `inh_Ikk` (entering as
  `A20 / inh_Ikk`) and the scale of the A20 imaging readout.
- **Relative measurements.** Blots and imaging give no absolute amounts. $X_2$ divides the IKK
  total and every IKK form by $\lambda$ and multiplies the IKK-catalyzed phosphorylation rates and
  the pIKK blot scale by $\lambda$; the IKK cycle is linear in IKK. NFκB and IκBα scale together:
  every form times $\lambda$; complex formation (second order), the readout scales and the A20
  transcription driven by nuclear NFκB divided by $\lambda$. The printed $X_3$ is this direction
  plus $X_4$ and $X_5$, hence it also moves nuclear volume and IκBα production.
- **Nuclear volume.** In $X_5$ `Vnuc` grows at fixed amounts, nuclear concentrations fall, and the
  rates reading them (transcription of IκBα and A20, nuclear complex formation) and the scale of
  nuclear NFκB grow to compensate.
- **A product.** `split_NfkIkb` appears only multiplied by `eta_split_pNfkpIkb` ($X_8$).

## Symmetry reduction

`symmetryReduction()` returns in `$trafo` a parameter transformation that removes the directions, for scalings
by fixing one coordinate per direction
([Methods > Gauge and reduction](methods-symmetries.html#gauge-and-reduction)).

```{r reduction, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
reduction <- readRDS("results/reduction.rds")
reduction
```

## Gauge fixing

The objective is flat along every orbit, so the fit fixes one moved coordinate per symmetry, the
gauge. This chooses units and leaves the fit unchanged. `model.R` fixes one parameter per scaling
at 1, 0 on log scale:

```{r gauge}
```

The `r inWords(length(gauge))` coordinates remove all `r inWords(length(types))` scalings if their
weight matrix is regular
([Methods > Gauge and reduction](methods-symmetries.html#gauge-and-reduction)):

```{r}
W <- t(vapply(symmetries$symmetries, function(X)
  vapply(names(gauge), function(cn) as.numeric(X$weights[[cn]] %||% 0), 0), numeric(length(gauge))))
dimnames(W) <- list(paste0("X", seq_len(nrow(W))), names(gauge))
W
det(W)
```

This is the gauge of Oppelt et al. [@oppelt2018model]: NFκB and IKK totals and nuclear volume set
the concentration units, so a concentration is a fraction of the moiety total; receptor and A20
transcript are in units of their production rates, the IκBα transcript in units of the translation
it drives, A20 in units of the A20 imaging scale. The reduction fixes other coordinates, a
different choice of units. [Optimization](guide-optimization.html) fits the remaining
`r length(setdiff(getParameters(p), names(gauge)))` parameters,
[Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html) checks which the data determine.

## Discrete symmetries

A locally identifiable model can still give the output of a parameter value at other, isolated
values: a discrete symmetry. `symmetryDetection(mode = "global")`, or `discrete = TRUE`, reduces
the directions, counts these values in the domain and reconstructs the maps between them where they
are rational functions of the coordinates; the search needs msolve. `discreteSymmetries()` runs it
on an earlier result.

In the reduced model of [Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html#reduced-model) some rates are
fixed and the resting state is given by the totals of NFκB and IKK; both enter the detection as
`trafo`, the other settings are those above. Code: `discrete.R`.

```{r discrete, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/discrete.rds", "discrete.R"))
```

```{r}
saved <- readRDS("results/discrete.rds")
discrete <- saved$discrete
discrete$info$discrete[c("count", "countFinal", "fundamentalDomain")]
swap <- discrete$discreteSymmetries[[1]]
swap[c("map", "level", "stateMaps")]
```

The search finds `r inWords(discrete$info$discrete$count)` parameter values with the output of a
generic one, the value itself and the image under the map, which exchanges the degradation rates of the A20
transcript and of A20 and leaves the other coordinates in place; `countFinal` says that no other
value is left. `exact` means proven by the map of the states: only the last stage of the
transcript changes, by the difference of the rates times A20, in units in which `build_A20` is 1.
The A20 branch is a linear chain from nuclear NFκB to the A20 readout, and A20 does not act back
on the network, so the readout depends on the two rates only through their sum and product. The
map moves no coordinate of the scalings, so it holds in the original coordinates as well.

The fundamental domain `degrad_A20 < degrad_RnaA20` keeps one of the two points.
`symmetryReduction(branch = )` gives a chart of this side in positive coordinates:

```{r fundamental, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
fundamental <- saved$fundamental
fundamental$trafo[c("degrad_A20", "degrad_RnaA20")]
```

`delta` is the positive difference of the two rates; a fit in this chart has one optimum where the
model without it has two
([Profile likelihood > Profiles in the fundamental domain](guide-profiles.html#profiles-in-the-fundamental-domain)).

Reference: `symmetryDetection()`, `symmetryReduction()`, `discreteSymmetries()`
